summary: Panel Component that uses vertex and pixel shaders to render directly to the screen. It is useful for pixel accurate UI because the rendered resolution adapts to display DPI scaling, panel variables are available to the shader, and the usual panel layout, interaction, look, children, drag/drop, extension, clone, and external tox controls still apply.

common_gotchas: Sampler declarations in GLSL must match the bound TOP dimensionality, such as sampler2D for a 2D TOP and sampler3D for a 3D TOP.
Display hides the panel and may incur layout processing; for simple overlays, adjust opacity instead.
Enable prevents interaction with the panel but does not mean the shader or panel network no longer exists.
Built-in Multi-Touch can interfere with scripts that handle touches through Multi Touch In DAT, so disable built-in handling when a custom touch pipeline owns events.
Panel anchors are normalized 0-1 values relative to the parent panel, while offsets and margins are absolute pixels.
Layer only orders panels at the same hierarchy level; sibling panels with equal layer values fall back to operator name ordering.
Background TOP fill and smoothness affect only the panel background, not the shader's own sampler uniforms.
external .tox reload options affect top-level custom and built-in parameters differently from node parameters inside the component.
Drag/drop callbacks can copy or modify operators in a temporary network, so treat drop scripts as behavior, not just metadata.
Use Info CHOP channels such as warnings and errors to diagnose cook and shader-panel state.
build_relevance: 2023.11280+ panel shader surface with DPI-aware rendering
